text:
incident-bot: [ALERT] p99 latency spike on /v1/chat/completions (route=chat:completion, model=mistral-7b) — p99 crossed 2.0s for 6m. Severity: page

alex: I’m on it. seeing tail at ~2.8s in the p99 heatmap.

maria: thanks. any affected customers yet?

jamal: quick look at logs: increased queuing on gpu-pool-a, burst from region-us-west-2. Not seeing errors, just long runtimes.

alex: product-ops, can you confirm if there were large traffic spikes (campaigns) right now?

product-ops: nope, no campaigns. small spike from a couple of PLG apps (~15% above baseline) but nothing crazy.

maria: routing note: we currently route by model preference then region. If pool saturated fallback to compact-7b-q4 exists but weight is low. Might need to nudge fallback.

jamal: if we shift a portion of traffic to compact-7b-q4 we should preserve latency SLO at the cost of slightly different outputs. recommend 20% reroute for 15m.

alex: agree. I'll flip a temporary route override. patch: `routes.chat.completions.override: {"mistral-7b": 0.8, "compact-7b-q4": 0.2}`

incident-bot: Action taken by alex: route override applied at 2000123465.

tina: adding a squelch on the p99 alert so we don't double-page during mitigation: set `squelch_window: 300s` and `noise_gate: 3` (for same incident)

maria: great. also enabling per-model p95/p99 panels on the live dashboard. link: https://redwood.internal/dashboards/latency-route-chat

jamal: pulled a sample of traces. root cause looks like a combination of larger-than-usual sequence lengths + one node in gpu-pool-a showing slow kernel selection (likely warmup/eviction).

alex: I've cordoned the problematic instance (gpu-a-12) and drained it. will monitor for improved tail.

incident-bot: instance gpu-a-12 drained by alex at 2000123478.

maria: on alert tuning: current p99 threshold = 2.0s global. Propose changing to per-route/per-model thresholds to reduce noise and be more actionable:
- chat.completions (mistral-7b): p95=0.9s p99=2.0s
- chat.completions (compact-7b-q4): p95=0.6s p99=1.2s
- embeddings routes: leave as-is

alex: also propose a traffic-aware p99 ratchet: if sustained load >1.2x baseline for 10m, temporarily widen p99 threshold by 25% and enable auto-fallback for 20% traffic. helps reduce pages during traffic surges.

tina: can we express that as alert config?

jamal: example snippet:```yaml
alerts:
  chat_completions_p99_mistral7b:
    metric: route.latency.p99
    threshold: 2.0
    scope: route=chat.completions,model=mistral-7b
    noise_gate: 3
    adaptive:
      enabled: true
      load_factor: 1.2
      widen_pct: 25
```

product-ops: sounds reasonable. need a note for customers that their models may be reweighted during mitigation windows.

maria: opened a follow-up ticket in infra: INF-8242 "Per-route p95/p99 alerting + adaptive widening" with tasks: dashboard panels, alert rule changes, doc updates, and a test harness.

alex: PR for on-call playbook draft: https://github.com/redwood/ops/pull/291 — includes steps: detect tail, apply route override, drain bad instance, squelch alerts, and create postmortem if impact > 5% requests.

incident-bot: Page acknowledged by sre-oncall at 2000123490.

sre-oncall: taking handoff. monitoring metrics now. p99 dropped to 1.5s after route override and drain.

tina: leaving the squelch in place for 20 mins, will remove after stabilization.

maria: next steps:
- Convert global p99 alert into per-route rules (INF-8242)
- Add per-model panels to latency dashboard (done in a basic way, will refine)
- Add adaptive widening as an experimental flag behind feature toggle
- Customer comms draft (product-ops)

product-ops: I'll draft a short note for customers using high-throughput PLG routes explaining automatic fallback policy and how to request pinning to a model.

jamal: metric note for post-incident analysis: collect `queue_time`, `kernel_selection_time`, `execution_time` and annotate with `pool_instance` so we can spot slow hosts automatically.

alex: setting a short-term config change: bump p99 squelch and enable override for next 30m. Will revert if things look normal.

incident-bot: incident cleared at 2000123590 (p99 steady < 1.6s for 6m).

maria: filing post-incident follow-up: assign to eng-runtime + eng-platform for root cause and alert redesign.

sre-oncall: handoff complete to maria at 2000123600. leaving notes in INF-8242.

alex: thanks team. quick wins look good — we'll reconvene in the follow-up ticket to finalize thresholds and rollout a more granular alerting config. :thumbsup:
